description:
Find real-world places and get each one back as a card: name, category, address, coordinates, phone, website, opening hours, status (open / closed / permanently closed), rating and review count. Pass `latitude` and `longitude` to search around a point — each card then carries its `distance` in metres — and `radius` to cap how far. When you only know the city, pass `user_location` instead. A query that names its own area ("ramen in Shinjuku") works without either.

USE FOR anything with a location: "coffee shops near me", "family-friendly restaurants", "museums in Lisbon", "is this place open on Sunday", "what's their phone number". The cards answer these directly — `search` would return pages *about* places that then have to be read.

Set `places.max_reviews` (0-5) when what reviewers actually wrote is the question — "is it good for groups", "do people complain about the wait". Off by default: review text is long, and `rating` plus `review_count` already come on every card.

Set `web_search.enable` to true when the pages discussing these places matter too (round-ups, articles). It is off by default: the places are the answer here, and the pages cost context.

Pass the caller's location when the question is relative to them ("near me", "nearby", "closest") or names no area at all — without it such a query is not limited to anywhere, and "near me" means nothing. A query that names its own area does not need it, and sending coordinates there is data the search will not use.

keywords: places, near me, nearby, restaurant, cafe, coffee shop, bar, hotel, museum, shop, store, address, directions, opening hours, phone number, rating, reviews, local, map

latitude.description: WGS84 latitude to search around. Must be sent with `longitude`.

longitude.description: WGS84 longitude to search around. Must be sent with `latitude`.

places.description: What to return per place. Omit to use the server defaults.

max_reviews.description: Review excerpts to return per place (0-5). Defaults to 0 — review text runs long, so ask for it only when what people actually said is the question. `rating` and `review_count` come back either way.

query.description: What to look for, e.g. 'coffee shops' or 'ramen in Shinjuku'. Max 500 chars.

radius.description: Keep only places within this many metres of the point. Requires `latitude` and `longitude`. Omit for no distance limit.

timeout.description: Request timeout in seconds (1-60). Defaults to 30s if unset.

user_location.description: Approximate location, for when coordinates are unknown. No `distance` is returned without coordinates.

web_search.description: Also return web pages about these places. Off by default — turn it on only when the pages themselves matter, since they cost context.

end_time.description: Upper bound for web results, ISO 8601.

exclude_domains.description: Drop web results from these domains. Max 1200, each ≤60 chars.

full_content.description: Cleaned page body per web result. Heavier than `highlight`.

include_domains.description: Only return web results from these domains. Max 1200, each ≤60 chars.

language.description: Languages to filter web results by, as ISO 639-1 codes.

start_time.description: Lower bound for web results, ISO 8601.

time_basis.description: Which timestamp the web-result time window filters against.

time_range.description: Relative time window for web results. The absolute range wins if both are given.

name: place_search
title: Place Search
